cards.explanation: The answer is True, friends. David says the one who walks with integrity also "practices righteousness" (Psalm 15:2). Notice the word practices. It's something you keep doing, like pressing a stamp into dough batch after batch. Nobody gets good at it by doing it once and taking a nap.

The answer is honesty that goes all the way down. David says he "…speaks the truth from his heart…" (Psalm 15:2). The truth starts down deep, so it isn't just a nice coat of frosting on top. What's inside is the same as what comes out.

The answer is True, friends. David says this person "…does no harm to his neighbor…" (Psalm 15:3). It's easy to be nice to strangers you'll never see again. Being kind to the people you keep running into, week after week? That's the real test.

The answer is False. David says he "…casts no scorn on his friend…" (Psalm 15:3). Scorn is looking down on somebody, and he doesn't do that to his friends. I'd say the friend who never rolls his eyes at you is worth more than a whole tray of warm cookies.

The answer is those who fear the LORD. David says he "…honors those who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 15:4). So he despises the vile and honors the people who fear the LORD. His respect goes to the right place.

The answer is False, friends. The psalm says he "…does not revise a costly oath…" (Psalm 15:4). Costly means keeping it hurts, and he keeps it anyway. It's like a cookie maker who promised a dozen boxes, found out it'd take all night, and kept the oven on.

The answer is that he lends it without interest. David says he "…lends his money without interest…" (Psalm 15:5). He lends it and doesn't add anything on top for himself. He helps the person and doesn't squeeze them.
The answer is refuses. David says he "…refuses a bribe against the innocent." (Psalm 15:5). The answer is no. He doesn't let money push around somebody who's innocent.

The answer is that he will never be shaken, friends! The psalm ends with "He who does these things will never be shaken." (Psalm 15:5). After that whole list, that's the closing promise. He stays steady.
